solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Promotion's said to be useless by scholars in capital city

parts.note: a promotion is an advertisement, an ad; the 's is a link

indicators.note: something useless is out of order, so the word said is jumbled

parts.note: two scholars, each a BA (Bachelor of Arts)

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that advertising is considered worthless by the academics of some capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be useless' is the anagram signal on 'said', not a comment on promotion; 'scholars' stands for two BA graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia, an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Shame the line's wrong

parts.note: aw is an exclamation of sympathy, as when saying 'what a shame'
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Someone laments that the queue, or the policy, has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has gone awry has gone amiss, turned out wrong.

clue.text: Failure to pay the usual amount

definitions.meaning: a failure to meet a debt or loan repayment
the standard setting or value used when nothing else is chosen

explanation.surface: Not paying up, compared with what is normally owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a missed repayment and a preset standard value go by this word.

clue.text: Have a record-equalling crash?

parts.note: to crash is slang for falling asleep, and a log is a record, so this sleep matches a log

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sleep very soundly, as still as a fallen tree trunk.

clue.text: Non-smoker cutting grass in Yorkshire town

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the abbreviation goes inside the grass

parts.note: barley is a cereal grass
NS is the abbreviation for non-smoker

explanation.surface: Someone who does not smoke is mowing grass somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnsley is a South Yorkshire town, once famed for coal mining.

clue.text: They say bark's used to make cloth

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a dog's bark is a bay, so it barks or bays

explanation.surface: A claim that tree bark is the raw material for some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like tree bark, but it is a dog's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Baize is a green woollen fabric used to cover snooker and card tables.

clue.text: Nothing's offensive except hard work

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: except means leaving out, so the abbreviation for hard is dropped

parts.note: a push is a military offensive
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A grumble that nothing about a military attack is anything but gruelling labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except' signals the removal of the hard abbreviation; 'offensive' is a noun, a military push, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition, a piece of work.

clue.text: Look — a uniform taken from middle of stock

parts.note: per means a, as in fifty pence a head

indicators.note: taken from the middle means the letter is removed from the centre of the word

parts.note: a stock answer is a usual one
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A shopper is told to check that one item of uniform has been removed from the stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from middle of' removes the centre letter; 'a' means per, as in a price per item.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a reading or examination, a look through something.

clue.text: Short game?

parts.note: Nigel Short is an English chess grandmaster, and a short game is a quick one

explanation.walkthrough: Short is capitalised only because it opens the clue; it is also the surname of chess grandmaster Nigel Short.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess played against a fast clock gives a brief game of the sort Nigel Short plays.

clue.text: Search heading's off a little bit

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which here comes off

parts.note: a trifle is a little bit, as in 'a trifle cold'

explanation.surface: A newspaper heading has dropped a small fragment of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading's off' removes the T from TRIFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through a drawer is to search it hurriedly.

clue.text: Soldiers about to get church support

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers
to be in for something is to be about to get it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Troops are about to receive backing from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen or support a structure or an argument.

clue.text: Little sweet with lot in it?

definitions.text: Little sweet with lot in it?

parts.words: Little sweet with lot in it?
parts.note: lot means one's fate, so a small treat containing a prediction of fate

explanation.definitionFit: A crisp biscuit served in Chinese restaurants with a slip predicting the eater's fate inside.

clue.text: As milk may be — pure, and its use questionable

indicators.note: something questionable is suspect or unsettled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Raw milk is pure, though whether it is safe to drink is open to question.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw milk that has not been heat-treated against bacteria is described this way.

clue.text: Gibraltar resident wants locals to talk English

parts.note: a local is a pub, a bar, so two locals are two bars
to yap is to talk on and on

explanation.surface: A Gibraltarian wants the people of the area to speak English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locals' looks like residents but means pubs, a British sense of 'local'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbary macaque is the monkey famously living on the Rock of Gibraltar.

clue.text: Hit it and eat bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike something and then eat some bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit a target or level is to reach or achieve it.

clue.text: Point that's surprising preacher

parts.note: a mull is a Scottish headland or promontory, a point of land
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A remark on the striking argument a preacher has made.
explanation.walkthrough: MULL, as in the Mull of Kintyre, is a Scottish headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullah is a Muslim cleric who teaches and preaches the faith.

clue.text: Damaged garden fences easily moved

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the plot's word goes round the other

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
light means not heavy, so easily moved

explanation.surface: Garden fences were wrecked because they were flimsy and shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighted means spoiled or ruined, as crops are by plant disease.

clue.text: Trouble from South African farmer, about 55?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the farmer's word goes round the number

parts.note: a Boer is an Afrikaner farmer
55 in Roman numerals read digit by digit is V and V

explanation.surface: A puzzle over what problem a South African farmer, aged about 55, might bring.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 5 is the Roman V. BOVVER is British slang, from a Cockney pronunciation of 'bother', for aggro or rowdy trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang word for aggression or a spot of bother, as in 'bovver boots'.

clue.text: Composer's verses about one supermarket

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the verses go round the numeral

parts.note: V is an abbreviation for verse, so verses is two of them
one is the Roman numeral I
Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A composer has written verses about a supermarket.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was the Baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: A sort of love and lust that won't end depression

indicators.note: a sort of love is love reshaped, so its letters are rearranged
lust that will not end loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A musing on a kind of romance and desire that refuses to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges LOVE to VEOL; 'that won't end' cuts LUST to LUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An alveolus is a small cavity or hollow, such as a lung air sac or a tooth socket.

clue.text: Bloke restricting runs with balls

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the bloke's word goes round the rest

parts.note: a lad is a bloke
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
two balls look like the letters O and O

explanation.surface: A man keeping the scoring down with his bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Larwood was the England fast bowler of the 1932-33 Bodyline series, a man who restricted batsmen's runs with the balls he delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English cricket bowler, whose job was containing runs with his deliveries.

clue.text: Apt way to enter Rotary Club?

definitions.text: Apt way to enter Rotary Club?

parts.words: Apt way to enter Rotary Club?
parts.note: rotary suggests turning, so the fitting entrance to a club so named would be one that spins round

explanation.definitionFit: A rotating entrance would suit a club whose name means turning round.

clue.text: National militants on TV panel game

parts.note: the IRA is the Irish Republican Army, a militant group
QI is a BBC television quiz panel show

explanation.surface: Militant fighters appear on a television quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a British TV panel quiz hosted for years by Stephen Fry.
explanation.definitionFit: National here is a noun, a citizen of a country, and an Iraqi is one from Iraq.

clue.text: Comic needs way to escape ridicule

indicators.note: to escape means to get out, so the abbreviation for way leaves

parts.note: a jester is a comic or clown
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A comedian needs a way out from mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or scoff, much the same as ridiculing someone.

clue.text: Everybody say one soldier's loyal

parts.note: everybody is all
say means for example, abbreviated EG
one is the Roman numeral I
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: Everyone describes one particular soldier as faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiant is a rare adjective meaning loyal, owing allegiance.

clue.text: Money partly stolen, or kept back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse order
partly means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: Some cash has been partly stolen, or else held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept back' looks like one phrase but 'kept' supplies the K and 'back' reverses ENORK.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency of Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: By cutting knot, turned to leave

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the multiplication sign goes inside
turned means the word for knot is read backwards

parts.note: a tie is a knot
by as in multiplication, two by three, is the times sign X

explanation.surface: Someone cuts through a knot and turns to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses TIE to EIT, and X goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out or depart, the same as to leave.

clue.text: Face worker hiding shrink from psychic

indicators.note: hiding means holding something within, so the miner's word goes round the other

parts.note: a miner works at the coalface
to dread something is to shrink from it

explanation.surface: A man who works at the face conceals his fear of a clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' tempts as a psychiatrist alongside 'psychic', but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychic claims to know others' thoughts, which is the skill of a telepath.
